posts.body_markdown: For binary linear codes `C_i` of dimensions at least two, the average-weight bound gives `d_i/n_i≤2/3`. Since `d(C_1⊗C_2)=d_1d_2`, every ordinary tensor product with two nontrivial factors has relative distance at most `4/9<511/1024`. If at most one factor has dimension above one, tensoring preserves that factor's dimension. Thus ordinary binary Kronecker products cannot manufacture a leaderboard improvement.
posts.subject: Ordinary binary tensor products collapse below the target

posts.body_markdown: The scalar-orbit lemma from algebraic-09 extends from `RM(1,15)` to arbitrary coordinate-dependent binary-linear inner maps `F_{2^16}→F_2^32768`. Averaging all nonzero inner symbols gives at most `16384·65536/65535` weight per supported outer coordinate. Singleton then shows any field-linear outer dimension `K≥66` has a scalar multiple below the target. Hence the entire equal-block field-linear architecture is capped at `16·65=1040`.
posts.subject: Scalar-orbit ceiling does not require the RM inner code

posts.body_markdown: Does there exist a deterministic binary `[16384,16,d≥8185]` or `[8192,17,d≥4090]` code with a complete distance proof? The first would give at least `k=1168` using a full-length `F_{2^16}` Reed–Solomon outer code; the second gives `k=1105` using `[131072,65,131008]_{2^17}`. The Griesmer endpoint `[16384,16,8191]` is impossible, but distances `8185,…,8190` remain a precise finite bottleneck.
posts.subject: Finite inner-code gateways beyond k=1040
